Experimental. A local account on a Juniper Junos device: its login class, password and SSH keys. Conn3x won't demote or delete the account it logs in as.

**Experimental.** Network devices are new, and this module may change between releases. It's tested against vJunos-switch 26.2R1.7 on a lab VM, not yet in CI.

Use `junos_user` to keep a local account on a Juniper Junos device: its login class, its password and its SSH keys. The change goes in like every Junos step does, once per device per circuit; see [`junos_config`](/modules/junos_config).

The password never reaches the device or state as text. Conn3x hashes `password_wo` on your machine, sends the salted SHA-512 hash as `encrypted-password`, and keeps only an HMAC of that hash in state, so a refresh can tell whether the account still holds your password without knowing it. A password changed on the device by hand shows as drift.

`ssh_keys` is the account's whole set of keys: a key that isn't listed is deleted. Leave it unset to leave the keys alone.

Conn3x won't delete the account it logs in as, or move it out of `super-user`. Removing the step deletes the account, as with every step that grants access, unless `on_remove = "forget"`.

## Example usage

Give the password from an ephemeral variable, so it stays out of state and plan files:

```hcl
step "alice" {
  junos_user {
    name        = "alice"
    class       = "operator"
    password_wo = "use-an-ephemeral-variable-here"
    ssh_keys    = ["ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIExampleKeyOnlyForDocs alice@laptop"]
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `class` | string | Yes | Its login class, such as super-user, operator or read-only. Junos requires one. |
| `name` | string | Yes | The account name. Not root. |
| `on_remove` | string | No | "delete" (default) deletes the account when the step goes, as with every step that grants access; "forget" leaves it. |
| `password_wo` | string | No | Write-only: the password, never kept in state. Conn3x hashes it here and sends the device the salted SHA-512 hash, as encrypted-password, so the password itself never reaches the CLI; a new value plans a change through password_hmac. Unset leaves the account's password alone. |
| `ssh_keys` | list of string | No | The account's public keys, one line each, such as "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... alice@laptop". Keys not listed are deleted; [] deletes them all, and unset leaves them alone. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_junos_user.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the account matched at the last refresh. |
| `password_hmac` | string | An HMAC of the hash the device should hold for password_wo, keyed outside state. A new password plans a change, and a refresh finds an account with another one out of sync. |
| `revision` | string | Changes each time Conn3x changes this on the host. Handlers watch it. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_junos_user` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.
